questions.question: Q: What does AO4 assess in GCSE Dance?

points.text: AO4 assesses the ability to analyse and evaluate dance, including professional works and own choreographic practice.

questions.question: Q: Explain the difference between describing and analysing a dance.

points.text: Describing means stating what you see (e.g. 'the dancers move in unison'); analysing means explaining how and why it works (e.g. 'unison creates a sense of unity reinforcing the choreographic intent').

questions.question: Q: Why must evaluation be supported by evidence?

points.text: Without evidence, evaluation is just opinion. AQA requires informed judgements backed by specific examples from the dance to show understanding.

questions.question: Q: How do the three appreciation skills of describe, analyse and evaluate work together?

points.text: You first describe what you see, then analyse how and why it works, and finally evaluate how effective it is — each skill builds on the previous one.

questions.question: Q: Why is using subject-specific terminology important in dance appreciation?

points.text: Accurate terminology shows precise understanding and communicates ideas clearly; vague language loses marks in the AQA written exam.
